# Lionheart Fixt 0.40.0 - the tinker

If you join Relican's Dark Wielders, he sends you to break the wizards who won't bow to him. There's
Quinn the herbalist, and you can talk him round or kill him.

There was meant to be a second name on that list: **Leonardo da Vinci.**

## Let me be straight about what this is

Unlike most of these releases, **I didn't restore anything here. There was nothing to restore.**

The quest existed as a name in a file and absolutely nothing else — no steps, no dialogue, no
recorded lines. I went looking three separate times because the name kept turning up in my own
notes, and every time the answer was the same: somebody typed a title during design and the idea
never went any further.

So this is me building it, not uncovering it. If that's not what you want from this mod, skip this
one — and the release after this will be back to genuine restoration work.

## Why you can't just kill him

Quinn you can murder. Leonardo you can't, and that turns out to be deliberate.

He's set to be effectively invulnerable — the same treatment the game gives children. And the
reason is the ending: **whether Leonardo is alive or dead when you reach the final confrontation is
one of the things the game's endings are built around.** There are separate endings for him living,
him dying, Galileo living, Galileo dying, and your own alignment, in every combination.

The developers made him unkillable because they needed him alive until the last act.

Which means the "or kill him" half of the Quinn quest is exactly the half that can't exist for
Leonardo. I could have torn out his protection and rewritten the endgame to match. I decided
against it — that's not a repair, it's a rewrite of somebody else's ending.

**So this is the one Dark Wielder job you cannot solve with a sword.** I think that makes it the
most interesting one.

## Talking him round

Three different ways in, and you only need one:

- **Talk well enough** and you can use his own words against him. He once told you that Wielders
  make pocket dimensions and that there are bigger ones out there. There's a man in one of those
  bigger ones who has been alone for an age — and no Wielder ever went down to get him.
- **Know enough magic** and you don't need to argue. You show him what you've already learned and
  ask whether his people could have taught you faster.
- **Or bring the ring** from last release's bargain with the mad enchanter. If you made that deal,
  you can tell Leonardo you've *been* down the well and met the man his order abandoned. It's the
  sharpest version of the argument, because it's true.

There's also a blunt, graceless attempt available to anyone, which fails.

## If he says no

He says no the way Leonardo would say no. He doesn't threaten you, he doesn't tell the Wielders,
and he doesn't stop helping you — his crossbow project and his directions still work exactly as
before.

He just tries to talk you out of it, once, and then lets you go:

> *"Relican does not want an apprentice. He wants an instrument, and an instrument is set aside
> once the work is finished. You will go where you choose, as every man must... But when you reach
> the bottom of it, remember that someone said so, and that the way back was never closed to you."*

Relican takes the refusal better than you'd expect, because he learns something from it anyway.

The whole job is **optional** — it's offered when you ask about it, not forced into the sequence. If
you never raise Leonardo's name, nothing changes.

## One thing you'll notice

**The new lines have no voice acting.** Leonardo is voiced for almost everything he says, so three
silent conversations will stand out. I can't fix that — the audio doesn't exist and never did.

It bothered me enough that I nearly didn't ship it. Flagging it honestly instead.

## Installing

Unzip and double-click **`Mod Manager.bat`**, then click the button that names the mod.

Works on **any save**, though you'll need to be on Relican's path to see any of it.

## If you play it

**The check that matters:** refuse him, then go back and use his shop, ask about the Wielders, and
check his crossbow quest. All of it must still work. A refusal that quietly broke his other content
would be the worst possible outcome here, and it's the thing I'd most want caught.

**And the judgement call:** does Relican's refusal to have him killed read like his own decision, or
does it read like the mod making an excuse? That's the bit I can't test.
